clue.text: The measure has no success but the Church gives a revealing performance

indicators.note: the dance is said to lack something, so those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: a measure is an old word for a dance, here the Spanish fandango
to make a go of something is to make a success of it, so go means success
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A dance number flops, but the Church steps in with a risqué show instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Measure is an old word for a dance, which hides the fact that a particular dance is meant. A fan dance is a burlesque act where the performer hides behind large feather fans.
explanation.definitionFit: The fan dance is a striptease-style act in which feathered fans conceal and then expose the dancer.

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A disguise for Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Lady was the nickname of Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister; here it splits into iron and lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat, something worn to cover the head.

clue.text: "Be not afeard: the isle is full of ______" (Tempest)

definitions.text: "Be not afeard: the isle is full of ______" (Tempest)

parts.words: "Be not afeard: the isle is full of ______" (Tempest)
parts.note: the missing word completes Caliban's speech in Shakespeare's play about the enchanted island

explanation.definitionFit: Caliban tells the castaways the island is full of sounds and sweet airs that give delight.

clue.text: Two kinds of fruit in this drink

parts.note: the apple is one fruit
the jack, or jackfruit, is a large tropical fruit

explanation.surface: A cocktail made with a pair of different fruits.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is short for jackfruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American apple brandy, a spirit distilled from cider.

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
templates are patterns to cut or copy from

explanation.surface: Someone who plans to examine designs.
explanation.walkthrough: Con as a verb meaning to study (con a lesson) is old-fashioned but crossword standard.
explanation.definitionFit: To contemplate doing something is to have it in mind, to plan or mean to do it.

clue.text: Rather put a sailor instead of a king in this small house

indicators.note: the sailor is put where the king was, so one piece swaps for the other

parts.note: to say you would rather is to say you prefer
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward's royal cipher
AB is an able seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a sailor over a monarch to live in a tiny home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' swaps the ER at the end of PREFER for AB. ER is usually the Queen, but here it is a king, Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a small factory-built dwelling, common in post-war Britain.

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
tan is a yellowish-brown colour

explanation.surface: A painter owns a coloured stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratan is a variant spelling of rattan, the palm whose stems make canes.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratan is a walking cane made from the stem of a climbing palm.

parts.note: a fly is an insect
a spy whose cover is blown has been discovered

explanation.surface: A spoiled bug is found out.
explanation.walkthrough: Blown as in a cover being blown: exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flyblown meat has fly eggs laid in it, hence spoilt or contaminated.

clue.text: Poet swallowing curious yarn in farming area

indicators.note: the poet takes the other letters inside, as if swallowing them

parts.note: a bard is a poet

indicators.note: curious means odd, so these letters come out strangely ordered

explanation.surface: A poet absorbing an odd tale while out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' gives NYAR, which 'swallowing' sets inside the poet after its third letter. The OCR misread yarn as yam.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnyard is the enclosed yard by a barn on a farm.

definitions.meaning: the grease that runs from roasting meat, kept for cooking

explanation.definitionFit: Dripping means soaking wet, and is also the fat collected from a roast joint.

clue.text: He has lasting qualities, of course

definitions.text: He has lasting qualities, of course

parts.words: He has lasting qualities, of course
parts.note: of course seems to mean naturally, but read it as on the racecourse: a horse with stamina for long races

explanation.definitionFit: A stayer is a racehorse with the endurance to last over longer distances.

indicators.note: adapting means altering to fit, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gallery showman reworking contemporary art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapting' rearranges TO MODERN ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrator shows how something works, putting it on display.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers
Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl taking up with a soldier is given the brush-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being rejected, but the bird is the definition: a reeve is the female ruff, a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The reeve is the name for the female of the ruff, a sandpiper.

clue.text: Nearly let trouble be for ever

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so these letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A plea that a near-miss of trouble should last for all time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges NEARLY and LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done eternally goes on without end, always.

clue.text: Effeminate attendant serving in a military train

parts.note: camp describes exaggerated, effeminate mannerisms
a follower attends on someone

explanation.surface: An effete servant attached to an army on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: A military train here is the column of people and baggage travelling behind an army, not a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp followers were the civilians who travelled with an army, supplying and serving its soldiers.

parts.note: loin is a cut of meat
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: A trimmed vestment for a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: The cloth is the clergy as a body, from their clerical dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth is a simple garment wrapped round the hips.

clue.text: Sailor king finds rising poverty in oil city

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: need is poverty

explanation.surface: A seafaring monarch discovers growing want in a petroleum town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NEED into DEEN. Aberdeen in Scotland is the hub of the North Sea oil industry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is Britain's oil capital, base for North Sea drilling.

clue.text: This means of transport is right if a car fails

indicators.note: a car that fails breaks down, so these letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Advice that this vehicle is the right one when a car breaks down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' rearranges RT with IF A CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft is a flying vehicle, a way of travelling.

clue.text: Pressing to the limit of safety, his hip goes on black ice

definitions.text: Pressing to the limit of safety

indicators.note: his hip is placed after, on top of, black ice

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a rink is a sheet of ice for skating
his can be rendered as man's, belonging to a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skating close to danger whose hip lands on black ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' puts the last two pieces after the first two, against the clue's order. Black ice is a hidden road hazard, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Brinkmanship is the tactic of pushing a dangerous situation to the edge of disaster to win concessions.

clue.text: Confusion is no good in a story

indicators.note: the letters for no good are placed inside the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A muddled tale with nothing worthwhile in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a muddle or knot, a state of disorder.

indicators.note: to be on board is to be inside the ship, so the food goes inside it

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and a steamship is SS
a tart is a food, a pastry

explanation.surface: Laying out a meal aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Being on board means being inside the ship, the convention that lets 'on' act as a container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out on a journey is to start it; starts means begins.

indicators.note: in an across clue, always placed on the bat comes after it

parts.note: a racket is the bat used in tennis or squash
e'er is poetic for ever, always

explanation.surface: A mobster who is forever swinging a bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, one thing on another sits after it. E'er, the poetic contraction of ever, loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs illegal rackets such as extortion, the business of a mobster.

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Backing for a tenancy agreement that is not standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' rearranges LEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that holds a painter's canvas upright.

clue.text: Church worker can do this as a chorister

definitions.text: can do this as a chorister

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A church employee who also sings in the choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Choristers intone or sing psalms and responses, the kind of singing a choir does.

indicators.note: an amendment alters wording, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parliamentary plea to vote through the change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the amendment' rearranges PLEASE. Pass here is the verb used of time slipping by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses goes by, as time passes.

parts.note: mighty means strong
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: A powerful king or queen who has yet greater authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stronger is being more powerful than another, the comparative of mighty.

definitions.meaning: a stinging weed with hairy leaves

explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irk them, and the nettle is the stinging hedgerow weed.

parts.note: arch as a prefix means chief or supreme, as in archbishop
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: The playful style of the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Ness is a headland or promontory, common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Archness is a knowing, mischievously playful quality in speech or look.
